messages:
maria: Quick design thread — I'm sketching a tiny ingest/gating API we can use to validate and atomically commit checkpoints before the streaming loader pulls shards into the hot cache. want quick sanity checks.

jon: nice. what are the invariants we need to preserve?

maria: main ones: 1) idempotent ingest (retries must not double-apply), 2) resumable streaming of large shard blobs, 3) a single canonical commit marker per checkpoint, 4) cheap per-layer checksums to detect corruption, 5) minimal changes for safetensors + sharded bundles.

kai: +1. also need backpressure signals so consumer (runtime) can refuse partially-validated checkpoints until commit.

sophie: can we avoid a full two-phase commit? that gets heavyweight with distributed catalog. maybe a lightweight lease + commit marker is enough.

maria: that's the idea. proposal: POST /v1/ingest-checkpoint -> returns a checkpoint-id and pre-signed streaming URL for each shard. ingest service stores a provisional metadata record (state: staging). clients upload shards in chunks to the provided URLs and report checksums via the API. once all shards verified, client calls POST /v1/ingest-checkpoint/{id}/commit which atomically flips state to committed. the runtime only sees checkpoints with state=committed.

jon: how do we make commit atomic given eventual consistency in the registry?

maria: use a single strong-write key in our metadata store (e.g., Dynamo conditional write on version) with compare-and-set. commit is write-if-version==staging-version. if write fails, client retries read->replay.

kai: what about resumable uploads? we need chunk offsets in the shard manifest and the ability to re-upload a failed chunk without redoing whole shard.

maria: plan: each shard is uploaded as chunked multipart with chunk metadata: {offset, length, chunk_checksum}. server stores chunk index and running digest (sha256). finalization verifies running digest == layer_checksum from manifest. clients may ask for next-offset via GET /v1/ingest-checkpoint/{id}/shard/{shard}/status.

sophie: nice. how does this work with safetensors where layers are contiguous in a file? do we require model format conversion first?

maria: we won't force conversion. ingest accepts both safetensors single-file or sharded safetensors. For single-file big safetensors we can still chunk at transport layer and compute per-tensor checksums by parsing headers during a staging pass (a staging worker can parse header, enumerate tensors, emit per-tensor checksums). that gives us ability to detect partial corruption at tensor granularity.

jon: deployment concern: staging pass doubles IO. can we make it optional for small checkpoints?

maria: yes — heuristic: if checkpoint size < 1GB skip tensor-level parse, only use file-level checksum. Otherwise staging-worker runs a parse/verify job. we'll surface a flag in API: "require_tensor_checksums": true/false.

kai: security: signed uploads + kms for checksum signing? we should sign commit metadata with KMS to prevent tamper.

maria: agreed. commit record will include a signature field signed with a deployment KMS key. runtime validates signature before promoting the checkpoint. prevents accidental or malicious write to registry.

sophie: how do we handle partial consumer compatibility? Example: runtime can only support certain quant profiles. Should we annotate checkpoints with "compatibility_tags" and have routing rules?

maria: yes add a compatibility section in metadata. ingest validates declared tags against a registry whitelist. runtime routing picks matching checkpoint variants. fallback is oldest compatible variant.

jon: what about migration of in-place committed checkpoints (e.g., we later re-index or add compact headers)? commit should be immutable but we might want to add derived artifacts.

maria: derived artifacts are separate objects with their own ids referencing the canonical checkpoint id. canonical commit is immutable. derived artifacts can be garbage-collected independently.

kai: any prototypes? can you drop a quick API example?

maria: sure, rough sketch:

```
POST /v1/ingest-checkpoint
body: {
  "model_name": "llama-70b",
  "format": "safetensors-sharded",
  "shards": [{"name":"shard-0000","size": 12_345_678}],
  "require_tensor_checksums": true,
  "compatibility_tags": ["quant-8bit", "kv-v1"]
}

response: {"checkpoint_id":"chkpt_abc123","shard_urls": {"shard-0000":"https://upload..."}}

# upload chunked with headers: X-Chunk-Offset, X-Chunk-Checksum
POST /upload/.. (chunks)

POST /v1/ingest-checkpoint/chkpt_abc123/commit
body: {"final_checksums": {"shard-0000": "sha256:..."}}
```

maria: ingest-bot: when commit succeeds, ingest-bot will emit a message to #eng-ml and to the catalog with the signed commit record.

ingest-bot: ingest-checkpoint chkpt_abc123 committed by maria at 2026-02-03T14:12:23Z :white_check_mark:

jon: sounds solid. one more: how do we prevent concurrent competing commits for same checkpoint id?

maria: the conditional write on metadata ensures only one commit wins. others get a conflict error and should fetch latest state. clients should be written to handle idempotent commit attempts.

sophie: operational: need metrics — time staging, upload throughput, commit latency, parse failures. also include a per-checkpoint "validation_logs" URL for debuggability.

maria: added. anything blocking? if no objections i'll put up a lightweight RFC and a small prototype with an S3-backed chunk store and Dynamo metadata. we can reuse existing safetensors parser from runtime for staging-worker.

kai: go for it. i'm happy to help on the resume/status endpoints.

jon: thumbs up from me.

sophie: +1. please include a migration plan for existing checkpoints (we should mark legacy ones as "unverified" and allow runtime to opt-in).

maria: noted, will add to RFC. thanks all.
